citations.quote: For any field $k$, the category of strong symmetric monoidal functors $\mathsf{Cob}^{\mathrm{cl}}_2\to\mathrm{Vect}_{\mathrm{fd}}(k)$ and monoidal natural transformations is equivalent to the category of finite-dimensional commutative Frobenius $k$-algebras and maps preserving multiplication, unit, comultiplication, and counit.

If $M$ is connected with genus $g$, $m$ incoming circles and $n$ outgoing circles, its value under the functor corresponding to $(C,\mu,\eta,\Delta,\epsilon)$ is $$ \Delta_C^{[n]}\circ H^g\circ\mu_C^{[m]}:C^{\otimes m}\to C^{\otimes n}, \qquad H:=\mu_C\Delta_C, $$

derivations.claim: Coordinatewise multiplication is associative and commutative with unit sum e_i; the pairing matrix is diagonal with entries w_i, so determinant product w_i is nonzero.
The displayed Delta and epsilon satisfy both counit equations, coassociativity and both typed Frobenius identities, checked on each idempotent basis element and extended by linearity.
The finite-dimensional commutative Frobenius algebra meets the root classification hypotheses; the resulting closed functor has the stated genus evaluation and cylinder action.

citations.quote: Fix an integer $r\ge1$ and let $A=\bigoplus_{i=1}^{r}\mathbb C e_i$, with coordinatewise multiplication $e_i e_j=\delta_{ij}e_i$ and unit $1_A=\sum_{i=1}^{r}e_i$. Choose weights $w_i\in\mathbb C^\times$ and define $\epsilon(e_i)=w_i$ and $\Delta(e_i)=w_i^{-1}e_i\otimes e_i$.
For the connected closed surface $\Sigma_g$ of genus $g\ge0$, it assigns $Z_A(\Sigma_g)=\epsilon(H^g(\eta(1)))$; the cylinder acts by $1_A$.

derivations.claim: For each idempotent, H(e_i)=mu(w_i^{-1}e_i tensor e_i)=w_i^{-1}e_i.
Applying the diagonal H repeatedly to eta(1)=sum_i e_i gives sum_i w_i^{-g}e_i, including g=0 by the identity convention.
Applying epsilon gives sum_i w_i^{1-g}; for g=1 each summand equals one, and the cylinder is the identity by the definition.

finite_checks.calculation: H^0 eta(1)=sum_i e_i, hence epsilon(H^0 eta(1))=sum_i w_i.

boundaries.evidence: The closed connected surface has no black boundary; its cup/handle/cap evaluation is given in the definition and used in step 3.1.

At g=1, w_i^(1-g)=1 for every i, so step 3.1 yields r.

There are no time or interval endpoints in this surface amplitude.

citations.quote: For any field $k$, the category of strong symmetric monoidal functors $\mathsf{Cob}^{\mathrm{cl}}_2\to\mathrm{Vect}_{\mathrm{fd}}(k)$ and monoidal natural transformations is equivalent to the category of finite-dimensional commutative Frobenius $k$-algebras and maps preserving multiplication, unit, comultiplication, and counit.

derivations.claim: The quotient has basis 1,x and multiplication ac+(ad+bc)x; it is a two-dimensional commutative unital associative algebra with nonzero nilpotent x.
The pairing matrix in basis (1,x) is [[0,1],[1,0]] with determinant -1, hence is nondegenerate.
The displayed Delta satisfies both counits, coassociativity on both basis elements, and both Frobenius identities on the four basis pairs.
Every maximal ideal contains x because the image of x is nilpotent in a field; the maximal ideal (x) exists, so the radical is nonzero.
The coefficient formula is Hermitian and the vectors 1+x and 1-x have squared values 2 and -2.
The finite-dimensional commutative Frobenius algebra satisfies the root classification hypotheses and therefore defines a closed-sector TQFT.
